sections.title: Form and flowering
sections.text: Biting stonecrop is a hairless, mat-forming succulent perennial with small, fleshy oval leaves close to the stems. It grows to about 10 cm high and spreads 10–50 cm. Star-shaped, five-petalled yellow flowers appear from May to July.

sections.title: Safety
sections.text: The Royal Horticultural Society warns that the sap can irritate skin and recommends protective gloves when handling it. Do not treat the peppery common name as evidence that the plant is safe to eat; the sources consulted do not establish a safe food use.
